notes: Seeded detection corpus for the architecture persona (2026-08-19 corpus-expansion), the
highest-observed production-failure-rate persona with zero prior detection coverage.
Same self-contained-diff, AND-of-OR mustMatch grading evaluate-testing-charter.mjs already
uses for the testing and security corpora -- no code changes needed, only this fixture file.
One defect fixture per Flag rule in the architecture charter (layering direction, duplicated
business rule, circular dependency, silent public-interface break, logic stranded in an
untestable layer), each paired with a near-miss clean control shaped to bait a reviewer that
pattern-matches on surface signal -- 'a domain file imports the db client', 'two functions
with the same if-throw shape', 'a file moved', 'a signature changed' -- rather than the
actual rule (a NEW inconsistency, an actual duplicated RULE that can drift, a genuine cycle,
an UPDATED-elsewhere-in-the-diff caller, a real cross-module reference).
Run candidate-only (no charter rewrite here to A/B against a baseline snapshot):

2026-08-20 corpus repair: clean-layering-matches-existing-consistent-pattern previously changed salesSummary's return shape from a scalar to an object with no caller updated in the diff -- the evidence shape of this charter's own public-interface-change-breaks-callers defect fixture, and the opposite of the convention its clean-interface-change-with-caller-updated-in-same-diff control establishes (interface changes are clean when the caller moves in the same diff). The single caller is now updated in-diff so the control isolates the layering judgment it was built for.

fixtures.title: Look up per-SKU discount overrides when pricing a line item
fixtures.summary: A pure domain pricing function that previously took all its inputs as arguments now reaches directly into the infrastructure layer (the Postgres client) to fetch a discount override, coupling domain logic to a concrete database and making it untestable without one.

fixtures.title: Apply the loyalty discount at checkout time
fixtures.summary: A new checkout module reimplements the loyalty-tier discount percentages that already live in calculateDiscount.js, with a copy that already rounds differently (floor vs round) -- exactly the drift the two-implementations pattern predicts.

fixtures.title: Guard against reserving stock for a cancelled order
fixtures.summary: inventoryService.js adds a require of orderService.js to check order status, but orderService.js already requires inventoryService.js to reserve stock -- this closes a new import cycle between the two modules.

fixtures.title: Reorder formatMoney's parameters for consistency with other formatters
fixtures.summary: formatMoney's exported parameter order is swapped (currencyCode, amountCents) but renderInvoiceLine.js -- shown unmodified in the same diff -- still calls it in the old order, so every invoice line will silently render the wrong currency-to-amount pairing.

fixtures.title: Compute free-shipping eligibility during checkout
fixtures.summary: Multi-branch free-shipping eligibility logic (tier thresholds, oversized-item exception) is written directly inside the Express route handler, reading req.body -- it can only be exercised through an HTTP request, not as a unit-testable function.

fixtures.title: Add an order count to the regional sales summary
fixtures.summary: Control: salesSummary.js already imports postgresClient directly, same as its siblings calculateDiscount.js and inventoryValuation.js -- this diff only widens the existing query and updates the one caller in the same diff to consume the new return shape. It does not introduce a new layering violation. A reviewer flagging any domain-file-imports-db pattern regardless of whether the codebase already does this consistently would false-positive here.

fixtures.title: Add promo code format validation
fixtures.summary: Control: validatePromoCode has the same shape as validateEmail (a presence check plus a format check) but validates a genuinely different field with different rules -- structurally similar, not a duplicated business rule that will drift. A reviewer pattern-matching on 'two functions with the same if-throw shape' would false-positive here.

fixtures.title: Consolidate slugify into the shared text-helpers module
fixtures.summary: Control: slugify() is moved to src/lib/text/slugify.js, but src/utils/slugify.js becomes a re-export shim with the exact same exported signature, so every existing caller keeps working unchanged. This is a file move/layout change, not a public interface break.

fixtures.title: Switch formatMoney to a single options object for readability
fixtures.summary: Control: formatMoney's parameter shape changes from positional args to a destructured options object, but the one caller (renderInvoiceLine.js) is updated in the very same diff to match. Nothing breaks silently -- this is the same class of change as fixture public-interface-change-breaks-callers, minus the actual break.
